title: Fall of Nineveh to Babylon and the Medes
summary: Fall of Nineveh to Babylon and the Medes
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

sorting_basis.note: PROVISIONAL: no CFAH, Ussher–Jones or Ussher date exists, so the sort uses Generations (Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), PDF p. 481): 612 BC. Pending owner decision (open question A8).

chronologies.note: pending CFAH reference (the CFAH series does not cover this period; no tier 1–4 date exists)

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 11 "Babylon Has Fallen (626–539 BC)", PDF p. 330 (printed p. 329)
chronologies.note: Nabopolassar with the Medes takes Nippur and Ashur (615 BC) and Nineveh; also pp. 321, 364.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "612 BC" (PDF p. 481): the same date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 19 "Babylon Has Fallen", PDF p. 481 (printed p. 467)
Herodotus, Histories 1.106 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 49 (PDF p. 51)
chronologies.note: After the Scythian period the Medes under Cyaxares recover their empire and take Nineveh. Generations dates the fall of Nineveh to 612 BC (provisional). That is inside the CFAH-derived reign of Cyaxares (635/634–595/594 BC), so consistent.
